best_for: Developers on Mac or Windows who want a quick visual Git client and are fine paying once for it after trying it.

points.title: One payment, three machines
points.text: A license is listed at USD 59.99 as a one-time purchase. It covers one user on up to three machines at a time, for personal or commercial use. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Try it before you buy
points.text: The site offers a free evaluation, so you can run it on real repositories first and pay only if it fits how you work.

points.title: Covers the daily Git work
points.text: Fetch, pull, push, commit and amend, branches and tags, cherry-pick, revert, merge, rebase, stashes and submodules are all built in. Interactive rebase, blame, reflog recovery, Git LFS and Git-flow are there too.

points.title: Line-by-line staging and image diffs
points.text: You can stage or unstage single lines, compare changes side by side, and diff images. That makes tidy commits easier when one file holds two unrelated edits.

points.title: No Linux build
points.text: Fork ships for macOS and Windows only. Linux users need a different client.

points.title: Windows keeps the history here
points.text: The Windows installer installs for the current user, x64 only, so no administrator rights are needed. The Windows listing keeps 35 versions; macOS lists only the current universal release, so downgrades there need another source.
